Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Trialistix is keen to move forward but we need a concise package for our legal and data governance teams before procurement can open the PO. Attached is the RFI matrix our privacy team prepared; key asks are in the "Transfers & Safeguards" and "Technical Measures" tabs. High priority items:

- Confirmation you can sign our DPA annex (we've highlighted clauses we usually push back on).
- Evidence of cross-border mechanisms used when EU controller data is processed in the US (DPF or equivalent).
- Network/crypto controls for KV cache and persistent logging.
- Retention / deletion mechanics for customer-scoped logs.

Can you provide a short deliverable ideally by EOD Monday (we're working to a sprint procurement window)? We're open to a short call if that helps.

Subject: Re: RFI: privacy appendix + DPF technical evidence request

Hi Olivia — appreciate the clear asks and the matrix. We're aligned on timeline and have pulled together a focused package to address the four bullets you called out. Quick summary up front:

1) DPA annex: Redwood can sign controller-friendly annexes; attached is our proposed DPA annex (redwood_dpa_annex_v1.pdf) with comments limited to operational clarifications. We can accept most of your redlines and have flagged two narrow edits around subprocessor onboarding and a mutual audit window (both negotiable).

2) Cross-border transfers / DPF: per your request we've prepared a short technical evidence workbook (dpf-technical-evidence.xlsx) that maps the dataflows, the contractual and technical safeguards we apply when routing EU-origin traffic to US-hosted inference pools, and our fallback routing behavior. The workbook includes the canonical legal basis mapping we use with European controllers.

3) Technical controls: the attached workbook + diagram (dataflow-diagram.png) call out KV cache scoping, in-memory-only default for ephemeral caches, AES-256-GCM encryption at rest for persisted artifacts, and tenant-scoped KMS keys for Private deployments. We've also included our log retention policy summary and an excerpt from the runtime manifest that shows how we rotate and evict session KV.

4) Retention & deletion: we support ephemeral session retention for hosted inference by default (30 days max for troubleshooting buckets unless customer opts-in for extended logs). For dedicated/private customers, you can specify retention via the Console or API; deletion requests are supported through an automated deletion workflow and audit record generation (see sheet 'Retention & Deletion' in the workbook).

I attached the three artifacts above and a short one-page note summarizing where we've accepted your redlines to the DPA annex. If it's helpful I can schedule a 30-minute call Monday morning to walk through the workbook with your privacy engineers.

Deliverables attached: redwood_dpa_annex_v1.pdf; dpf-technical-evidence.xlsx; dataflow-diagram.png

Next steps: if the materials look reasonable, the practical path is (a) confirm any final DPA edits, (b) we share a DocuSign link for the annex, (c) procurement issues PO. Happy to accelerate if needed.

Respectfully,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference

Morning all — quick legal/controls check from my side after a pass over the annex and evidence workbook:

- DPA Annex: we can concede to Trialistix's requested data deletion SLA with the caveat that deletion for backups follows our documented restore window (we've added a parenthetical explaining timelines). We pushed a minor clarification to the subprocessor list cadence (quarterly disclosure vs immediate notice for critical changes) — happy to make that immediate notice if Trialistix requires it; flag for decision.

- DPF mapping: the workbook includes references to the contractual mechanisms we use (standard contractual clauses + supplemental DPF notes) and the operational routing policy. For customers requiring a full DPF dossier we can provide a separate attestation packet under NDA.

- Crypto & key custody: for Hosted API customers, keys are managed in Redwood-managed KMS with tenant-scoped encryption keys; for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and provide HSM integration notes. We included an example KMS key policy snippet in the workbook.

Marcus — please confirm procurement path for signing (DocuSign link provided in Marcus' note) and whether we want to pre-approve the two minor edits I mentioned before sending back to Olivia.

Laura — can you add the brief retention/exceptions note to the workshop workbook (one paragraph) so Olivia's team has a single page explaining troubleshooting vs customer-requested log retention?

Thanks,
Karthik
VP Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
